viz_reviews.summary: Two labelled per-actor rings with the feedback nodes in the gap between them make the competing-loops shape recognisable at a glance; cross-loop feeds_back arrows show where the loops touch. Orientation diamonds carry gold idea rings in the TBPN example. Metrics clean for both examples; stats match graph.json; panels correct.

notes: Research step: John Boyd's OODA loop, developed from Aerial Attack Study (1964) and Energy-Maneuverability theory, formalised in the briefings Patterns of Conflict and The Essence of Winning and Losing (1996). Four phases Observe, Orient, Decide, Act, but the real content is that Orientation is the big outer loop: it is shaped by genetic heritage, cultural tradition, previous experience and new information, and it both filters observation and feeds implicit guidance and control directly to action, bypassing explicit Decide. Boyd's operational claim is not 'be fast' but 'operate inside the adversary's OODA loop' - generate a rapidly changing environment the adversary cannot orient to, so his decisions are answers to a world that has already moved. Common misuse: reading OODA as a tidy four-box sequential cycle (a PDCA lookalike), dropping the orientation feedback arrows and the adversary entirely. Design decision for this framework: model TWO competing actors' loops so that one actor's action node feeds the other actor's observation node, and cycle-time asymmetry is visible. | Scout returned three candidates: (1) Google vs OpenAI Gemini 3 code red 2025-12-02, (2) Meta vs OpenAI comp raid 2025-06-30, (3) Paramount vs Netflix counter-bid 2025-12-09. Chose (1): it is the only candidate where both actors' loops are shown closing on each other across two turns (ChatGPT 2022 -> Google's code red -> a decade of TPUs -> Gemini 3 -> OpenAI's code red), and the cycle-time asymmetry is stated in units on the record (a decade of silicon vs an answer due now). (3) would have duplicated the episode already used by inversion-premortem. | Validator: 0 errors, 0 warnings. Shortened two classic labels (c_s_or2, c_m_lose) to stay inside 40 chars before the scaffold commit. | Design decisions: two interlocking rings, one per actor, actor node at each ring centre with performed_by spokes; idea_bearing_slot is `orientation`, because for OODA the exploitable thing is the blind spot in a rival's filter, and three derived orientation nodes carry `idea` (g_orient, o_or_bench, o_or_subs). | SPEC 3 split rule is demonstrated on OpenAI's orientation: o_or_stated is a FACT node in the orientation slot (Mark Chen's own after-the-fact admission about reasoning vs pre-training), and o_or_bench / o_or_subs are the derived halves the speakers never state. | te20 (o_dec_personalize -> o_act_chen, 0.55) is deliberately below 0.65: the action slot on OpenAI's side has only a public promise inside the two-week window, and the rationale says so. | Resume 2026-09-10: the first viz builder was killed by a usage limit before reporting. The resuming parent judged its uncommitted work: the graph.json diff touched only region x-ranges, node pos and ten labels (c_sabre, c_mig, c_s_or2, c_s_dec, c_s_fb, c_m_or, c_m_dec, o_dec_subs; c_m_ap and c_m_act had been shortened by the orchestrator commit 45f7e43), index.html rendered with clean metrics, so it was committed as viz iteration 1 and a fresh critic passed it (4/4/4/5). Critic suggestions (nudge c_s_dec, g_obs_compute, o_dec_pretrain, c_m_lose; a circular guide per actor) were not applied because the verdict was pass; a later polish could take them. | Reconcile: stripped graph.json identical to the scaffold commit; README bold labels updated to the final labels (labels only, no content change, so no content commit); all relative links and the wikipedia link resolve; prose is about 2,540 words excluding the per-edge enumeration paragraphs in the What-the-LLM-added sections, which are decomposition entries in prose form. Final review: g_orient's idea rewritten to Google's side (the ads-machine tie as a wedge for a subscription-native assistant) so it no longer duplicates o_or_subs's monetisation-gap idea; README opportunity section updated.
